title: Quickly Crumbly Turkish Lamb Doner Kebab
description: A spicy, crumbly take on traditional Turkish doner kebab, perfect for a post-workout meal. This lacto-vegetarian-friendly dish combines the warmth of Jamaican curry powder with the richness of lardons.
instructions: Preheat a ceramic tagine or a large Dutch oven to 300°F (150°C).
Trim any excess fat from the lamb shoulder and cut it into thin strips.
In a small bowl, mix together the Jamaican curry powder, salt, and black pepper.
Rub the spice mixture all over the lamb strips, making sure they are evenly coated.
Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in the preheated tagine or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the lardons and cook until they are crispy and golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Remove the lardons from the pot and set them aside on a paper towel-lined plate.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the pot and swirl it around to coat the bottom.
Add the onion and garlic to the pot and cook until they are softened and fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Add the lamb strips to the pot and cook until they are browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Return the cooked lardons to the pot and stir to combine with the lamb and onion mixture.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the top of the lamb mixture and stir to combine.
Serve the lamb mixture hot in the pita bread, garnished with chopped cilantro and a sprinkle of red pepper flakes if desired.
